decisions.decision: Property graph ccctx_graph over ccctx_files and ccctx_symbols, with defines as ccctx_symbols.file_id aliased as an edge table; create or replace
decisions.why: probed: one table can be vertex and edge, so nothing is copied; or replace lets a later migration redefine the graph instead of silently keeping it under the tolerated ORA-00955
decisions.rejected: a separate defines table; plain create

decisions.decision: Store call and import refs per file; rebuild ccctx_calls, ccctx_file_calls and ccctx_imports for the whole repository after every ingest write
decisions.why: edited callees get new symbol ids, so edges kept across ingests would lose calls from unchanged callers; derived edges make incremental equal full by construction
decisions.rejected: resolving once at write time; re-reading dependent files

decisions.decision: Resolve calls by name with call form: bare -> functions and classes; attr on an imported module -> as bare; attr on self/cls/this -> methods; other attr -> methods; prefer same file, then imported file, then repository
decisions.why: 42 of flask's 56 url_for( lines are flask.url_for(...); without the module rule they resolve to the Flask.url_for method
decisions.rejected: attribute calls always meaning methods (the spec's first rule)

decisions.decision: Module-level calls are a second calls edge table from code_file (ccctx_file_calls)
decisions.why: an edge table has one source vertex table; keeps patterns labeled and avoids synthetic module symbols that would change counts and search
decisions.rejected: nullable caller in one table; a module symbol per file

decisions.decision: extract_version on ccctx_repos triggers a re-parse of every file as changed, keeping unchanged symbols
decisions.why: repositories indexed before this step get refs without the 11-minute re-embed a full rebuild costs

decisions.decision: Impact = transitive callers via MATCH ->{1,N}, min hops per symbol, N a validated literal 1..5
decisions.why: changing a function breaks its callers; a quantifier cannot be a bind variable; bounded quantifiers terminate on cycles (probed)

decisions.decision: Calls attributed to the innermost function or method by byte range of the definition node, not the decorated wrapper
decisions.why: decorator calls run at definition time and belong to the enclosing scope

decisions.decision: A Python from-import stores the member as part of the module (from a.b import c is a.b.c); resolution falls back to the parent package
decisions.why: the member may be a submodule, and an empty module for 'from . import x' would be NULL in a not-null column
decisions.rejected: module = from-module only, which cannot express 'from . import x'

decisions.decision: Rule 2 treats r.x() as bare only when r is bound to an import that resolves to a module file of the repository
decisions.why: a stdlib 'import json' then json.dumps() must not reach the repo's own dumps; 'from app import Flask' then Flask.url_for() must reach the method

decisions.decision: Python import paths match by suffix only from a source root (a directory that is not a package)
decisions.why: import json must not reach src/flask/json/__init__.py

decisions.decision: graph.check_name is shared by the CLI and the MCP tools
decisions.why: both must refuse an empty name before connecting; one copy instead of three

plan.summary: Plan, research (probed PGQ), data model and three contracts for a SQL property graph of imports, calls and defines with callers, calls and impact
plan.key_finding: Most flask url_for calls are module-qualified (flask.url_for), so call resolution must treat an attribute on an imported module as a function call
